title: Rounded rectangular rod
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and extends to (0.75, 0.0). The second line runs from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0117). The third line moves from (0.75, 0.0117) to (0.0, 0.0117), and the fourth line completes the loop by connecting (0.0, 0.0117) back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles as initially set, and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch along its normal by 0.0586 units, ensuring no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Finally, create a new solid body using the extruded two-dimensional sketch. The dimensions of the resulting rounded rectangular rod are 0.75 units in length, 0.0117 units in width, and 0.0586 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0.0117).lineTo(0, 0.0117).close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the rod
rod = sketch.extrude(0.0586)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = rod

lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0117, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0117, 0.0586) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0586) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
